messages:
Maya: Quick sync — Glenwood POC kicking off tomorrow morning. Customer will test two variants: `glenwood-13b` (fp16) and `glenwood-13b-8bit`. Can we confirm both are in our catalog and compatible with Dedicated (A100) and Private (VPC) deployments?
Emma: I can do an inventory check. My quick note: 8bit variant may need different kernel/quant path. Will flag if we need a custom build. What SLA/latency targets did they give?
Maya: They want sub-150ms p95 for short prompts (~128 tokens) and 500ms p95 for 1k token inference. Also KV cache must be enabled.
Raj: KC — on A100 both variants should run but 8bit requires the quantized runtime path. We have that on Hosted + Dedicated, but for Private we need to ensure their infra has the right CUDA/cuBLAS versions. I can check image compatibility.
Raj: Also note: KV cache behavior differs for 8bit on older kernels; we may see ~5-10% throughput delta.
Emma: Link to our internal matrix: https://intra.redwood.dev/model-catalog/compat — I'll add Glenwood entries and mark caveats.
Oliver: Heads-up on security Qs from procurement: they want confirmation on KMS integration (customer-managed keys), data at rest encryption, and audit log retention. They also asked whether Private supports air-gapped setups for FIPS components.
Maya: They pushed a short security questionnaire in the RFP — can we get draft answers today?
Oliver: I'll take the security Qs. Short answers: yes for cmk (via KMS/HSM), yes for encryption at rest/in transit. Air-gapped + FIPS: supported in our Private on-prem package but needs legal + infra signoff. I'll draft.
Emma: For pricing: Glenwood is latency-sensitive so likely they'll want Dedicated reserve. Ballpark: 2x A100 reserved nodes + burst capacity. Rough monthly commit estimate = ~$35k-$60k depending on tokens and burst. Will produce an options table.
Maya: Customer asked if quantized variant reduces cost and how we bill tokens for 8bit quant — same token unit pricing?
Raj: Token billing unchanged. Quant reduces GPU utilization so effective $/token drops. I'll run a quick perf/est with recent benchmark harness and share numbers.
Raj: Quick run command I used locally: ```bash
./bench_run --model glenwood-13b-8bit --seq 1024 --batch 4 --kv_cache on
```
Emma: If we need to enable a compatibility flag in their Private deployment, I'll open a request to eng-runtime. @raj can you paste exact runtime flag?
Raj: Flag is `--enable-quant-kernel-v2`. For Private, ops will need the image tag `redwood/runtime:quant-v2-2026-03`.
Maya: Timeline-wise: POC starts tomorrow. Goal: 3-day smoke tests (latency/cost/regen). Can we promise a staging endpoint + credentials by EOD?
Emma: I can provision Hosted staging endpoint in ~2 hours for baseline tests. For Dedicated/Private staging we'll need infra lead involvement; may take until EOD.
Oliver: I'll attach the draft security answers in this thread when ready. Also note they require a signed DPA before sending any customer data to Hosted.
deploy-bot: Deployed staging-hosted/glenwood-smoke @ 2026-03-21T10:24:11Z :rocket:
Maya: Awesome, thanks. Next steps: Emma to confirm catalog compatibility and staging endpoint link; Raj to run perf estimates and list any kernel caveats; Oliver to post security Q answers; I'll consolidate and send to Glenwood by noon. :thumbsup:
Emma: Catalog: confirmed `glenwood-13b` (fp16) and `glenwood-13b-8bit` (quant) present. Added note: Private needs `quant-v2` image. Staging link: https://staging.redwood.dev/glenwood-smoke
Raj: Perf numbers (quick): fp16 ~ 120ms p95 @128 tokens on A100, 8bit ~ 140ms p95; cost delta ~ -28% tokens/sec for fp16 -> 8bit yields 20-30% GPU $ savings in our test. I'll attach detailed CSV in follow-up.
Oliver: Security Qs draft attached: "KMS: supported (customer-managed), Data retention: configurable, Audit logs: stored 13 months (enterprise packs longer). Air-gap: available for Private with professional services." Uploading doc now.
Maya: This is great — I'll send the POC kickoff email with the staging link and our answers. If anything else blocks today ping me here.
Emma: :thumbsup:
Maya: Thanks team.
